Shop Storefront Brief · Issue 2

Apple asked a US court for 15% on link-outs. That is a proposal, not your US rate.

2026-08-24 · Fortune Insight, LLC · Operator intel for indie iOS teams. This page is a discussion note, not legal advice, and not investment advice. Confirm every rate in App Store Connect and your contracts.

What Apple filed

On 2026-08-13 Apple filed a court-ordered proposal in Epic v. Apple asking what it wants to charge when a US app links out of the App Store and the user pays on the web. That filing is not a Connect toggle and not a published US storefront rate. Treat 15% as Apple's ask.

Proposed US link-out commissions (public reporting)

Copied from public reporting as a worksheet. This is Apple's proposed ask in court, not a rate you can select in Connect today. Confirm in Connect before you change pricing or checkout.

Category Proposed commission
Standard 15%
Video / News / Mini Apps and subscription renewals 10%
Small Business Program 5%

What this is not

Do not rebuild US checkout this week because a headline said 15%. The EU 2026-10-01 fee table is Issue 0 — do not paste that worksheet onto US SKUs.

A court filing is a legal position, not a product launch. Until Apple publishes US storefront terms and you accept them in Connect, your current US IAP and link-out rules are whatever your contract and Connect say today.

Also on the calendar

  • September 2026: social-media questionnaire required — see Apple Developer News (2026-07-09).
  • Korea GRAC notes (2026-08-12): optional read for teams shipping in Korea — Apple Developer News.

What an indie can do this week

  • If you only sell US IAP inside the App Store: ignore the 15% headline for now. Nothing in Connect changed because of the filing.
  • If you run link-out checkout in the US: read the filing summaries, but do not reprice until Apple publishes and you accept new terms.
  • If you sell in the EU: keep the Issue 0 1 Oct date on your calendar. US and EU fee paths are separate worksheets.
  • Complete the September social-media questionnaire if Apple flagged your app — that is a compliance task, not a fee change.

Sources: 9to5Mac · MacRumors · The Verge · TechCrunch · Apple Developer News (social-media questionnaire) · Apple Developer News (Korea GRAC)
